planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Miracle is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction prized for foliage that shifts color through the growing season.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in dappled or partial shade; Miracle is a compact coral bells cultivar whose ruffled leaves emerge fiery orange-red flushed with purple in spring, mellow to amber-bronze through summer, and deepen toward plum-purple as nights cool in fall, giving a single plant three distinct looks across the season. The tight, tidy mound holds its shape well and resists flopping even in humid weather. Slender wiry stems carry small cream-white bells above the foliage in late spring, best left in place for pollinators. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the color display vigorous.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Mocha is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction grown for its large, dark, ruffled leaves.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Mocha bears large, rounded, deeply ruffled leaves in a rich matte chocolate-brown with subtle burgundy undertones that read almost black in low light. The vigorous, mounding habit fills space quickly and holds its dark color through summer heat better than many purple-leaved types. Tall, wiry stems carry small greenish-white flowers well above the foliage in early summer, though the leaves remain the main attraction all season. Cut back tattered leaves in early spring to refresh the mound before new growth emerges.

common_name: Carnival Peach Parfait Heuchera (Apricot Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Peach Parfait is a Proven Winners Carnival series coral bells grown for warm apricot foliage tones.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Carnival Peach Parfait produces ruffled leaves that emerge peachy-orange flushed with rose, settling into a soft caramel-apricot tone that pairs well with chartreuse or burgundy companions in a mixed shade container. The dense, compact mound is well suited to smaller borders and pot culture where its warm coloring can be viewed up close. Airy sprays of small pale flowers appear in late spring above the foliage but are secondary to the leaf display. Provide steady moisture and good drainage, and divide crowded clumps every few years to maintain a tight habit.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Gotham is a Proven Winners introduction with dark, silver-marbled foliage and strong heat tolerance.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Gotham carries near-black leaves overlaid with a bold pewter-silver marbling along the veins, creating a moody, metallic effect that darkens further with cooler fall temperatures. The vigorous mound holds its dramatic coloring through summer heat and humidity better than many dark-leaved types, making it a reliable anchor for shade containers or as edging against lighter foliage. Small ivory flowers rise on thin stems in late spring, adding little visual weight compared to the foliage. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep growth vigorous.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; Lipstick is a Heuchera sanguinea cultivar selected for its vivid red bell-shaped flowers.

directions: Plant in gritty, well-drained soil in partial shade; Lipstick forms a low mound of scalloped, matte green leaves with mottled silver veining, but its main draw is the profusion of brilliant lipstick-red, bell-shaped flowers held on slender wiry stems well above the foliage from late spring into summer. The long-blooming flower display is a strong hummingbird and pollinator draw and holds up better to some direct morning sun than most dark-leaved hybrids. Deadhead spent flower stems to encourage rebloom and prevent the clump from looking tired by midsummer. Divide every three to four years in spring to renew vigor and flowering.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Snow Angel Heuchera (Pink and Cream Variegated Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Snow Angel is a classic variegated coral bells cultivar best protected from strong afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Snow Angel is a long-grown variegated coral bells with green leaves irregularly marbled in cream and white, often flushed rose-pink along the margins and especially vivid during cool spring and fall weather. Because the white variegation can scorch, it performs best with protection from hot afternoon sun, making it well suited to woodland edges and north-facing beds. Airy, small white flowers appear on thin stems in late spring above the foliage clump. Remove any leaves that revert to solid green promptly to keep the variegation strong, and divide every few years in spring.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Hercules is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction bred for oversized, vigorous foliage.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Hercules lives up to its name with extra-large, ruffled leaves noticeably bigger than most coral bells, colored deep purple-black beneath a silvery-pewter overlay that traces the dark veins. The robust, fast-filling mound makes an effective focal point or large-scale ground cover where a bolder texture is wanted in the shade garden. Sturdy stems carry small pale flowers above the foliage in late spring, secondary to the striking leaf size and color. Give it extra room compared to standard cultivars and divide only when the clump becomes congested, typically every four to five years.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

common_name: Purple Petticoats Heuchera (Ruffled Purple Coral Bells)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Purple Petticoats is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction known for its deeply crimped, ruffled foliage.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Purple Petticoats forms a mound of glossy, deep purple-black leaves so tightly crimped and ruffled along the margins that they resemble gathered fabric, giving the plant strong textural interest even without flowers. The color holds well from spring through fall and deepens further as temperatures cool. Slender stems carry small white flowers above the foliage in early summer, a minor accent compared to the dramatic leaf texture. Site where the ruffled detail can be appreciated up close, such as along a shaded path edge, and divide congested clumps every three to four years.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Binoche is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with refined, silver-etched purple foliage.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Binoche bears ruffled, deep purple-black leaves etched with a fine silver overlay that follows the vein pattern, giving the foliage a refined, almost metallic sheen. The neat, well-proportioned mound stays tidy without flopping, making it useful for edging a shaded border or filling a container alongside chartreuse companions for contrast. Slender stems carry small pale flowers above the foliage in late spring. Provide consistent moisture and sharp drainage, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Regina is a Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with large, silvery, dark-veined foliage.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Regina produces large, rounded leaves in bright silvery-white overlaid on a purple-black base, with fine dark veining and rich burgundy undersides that show at the leaf edges. The bold, pale foliage brightens dim corners of the shade garden and reads well from a distance, unlike many darker cultivars. Wiry stems hold small ivory flowers above the foliage in late spring, a modest accent to the striking leaf color. Give the clump ample room to reach full size and divide every four to five years once congested.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Interstellar is a newer Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with bold silver-over-purple foliage.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Interstellar carries deep purple-black leaves overlaid with a bright, star-patterned silver marbling that radiates outward along the veins, giving the mound an eye-catching, almost luminous quality in low light. The compact, vigorous habit fills in quickly and holds its color well through summer heat. Small pale flowers rise on thin stems above the foliage in late spring. Pair with chartreuse or gold companions for contrast, and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to keep the display fresh.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Heuchera for Southern Gardens
